title: Reading records safely
description:
Read records like `Ada,36,ada@example.org` from lines of text, collecting errors instead of crashing:

```python
class InvalidRecord(Exception): ...

def parse_record(line): ...      # -> (name, age, email); raises InvalidRecord with a message
def load_records(lines): ...     # -> (records, errors); errors are "line N: <message>", N counting from 1
```

`parse_record` checks, in order, and raises `InvalidRecord` with these messages:
- not exactly three comma-separated fields: `"expected 3 fields, got N"`
- an empty name (after stripping spaces): `"missing name"`
- an age that is not a whole number: `"age is not a number: <text>"` (use `int()` and catch its `ValueError`, re-raising as `InvalidRecord` with `from`)
- an age outside 0-150: `"age out of range: <age>"`
- an email without exactly one `@` with text on both sides: `"invalid email: <text>"`

Fields are stripped of surrounding spaces. `load_records` skips blank lines (they are not errors).
hints: `email.partition("@")` splits at the first `@`; a valid address has text before it, an `@`, and text after it that contains no further `@`.
